sections.title: Basic Concept of Question Tags
sections.content: Question tags are short questions added at the end of a sentence to seek confirmation or agreement. If the main sentence is positive, the tag is negative, and if the main sentence is negative, the tag is positive.

sections.title: Helping Verb According to Tense
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the tense of the main sentence. Step 2: Use the same tense helping verb in the tag. Step 3: Use a negative tag for a positive sentence and a positive tag for a negative sentence. Example: She is happy, isn't she?

sections.title: Changing Noun to Pronoun
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the subject of the sentence. Step 2: Replace the noun with the correct pronoun. Step 3: Use the same pronoun in the tag. Example: Ram is playing, isn't he?

sections.title: Special Rule for 'I am'
sections.content: Step 1: If the sentence begins with 'I am', the normal rule does not apply. Step 2: Use 'aren't I' in the tag. Step 3: This is a fixed rule. Example: I am late, aren't I?

sections.title: Basic Examples
sections.content: You are ready, aren't you? They finished the work, didn't they? She will come tomorrow, won't she?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Using the wrong helping verb. 2. Not converting the noun into a pronoun. 3. Not reversing the positive and negative structure.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: To form a question tag, three things are necessary: the correct helping verb, the correct pronoun, and a positive-negative balance. With 'I am', the tag is always 'aren't I'.

tricks.title: Positive Sentence Rule
tricks.explanation: If the sentence is positive, the tag will be negative.
tricks.example: She is a teacher, isn't she?

tricks.title: Negative Sentence Rule
tricks.explanation: If the sentence is negative, the tag will be positive.

tricks.title: Helping Verb Copy Trick
tricks.explanation: Repeat the helping verb from the main sentence in the tag.

tricks.title: Pronoun Conversion Trick
tricks.explanation: Always convert the noun into a pronoun.

tricks.title: Past Tense Shortcut
tricks.explanation: In simple past tense, use did/didn't.
tricks.example: She finished the work, didn't she?

tricks.title: I Am Special Rule
tricks.explanation: With 'I am', the tag is always 'aren't I'.

tricks.title: Check Subject Last
tricks.explanation: While forming the tag, check the subject pronoun at the end.
tricks.example: The boys are ready, aren't they?
